key_insight: Large AI models can turn solid electrolyte discovery from slow, intuition-driven screening into a closed-loop, self-improving process that combines literature mining, candidate generation, multiscale simulation, and experimental validation.
engineering_relevance: This framework could accelerate the design of safer, higher-performance solid-state batteries by jointly optimizing ion transport, stability, mechanics, and interfaces.
method: Use MLIPs to bridge DFT accuracy with long-timescale ion migration and structural dynamics.
Use LLMs to mine literature, generate hypotheses, and support scientific reasoning.
Integrate AI selection, uncertainty-aware simulation, and experiment in a closed-loop autonomous workflow.
evidence_signal: The paper is a framework and perspective rather than a benchmark study, grounded in the known bottlenecks of fragmented data, limited simulation transferability, and slow experimental iteration.
watch_item: Real-world deployment will depend on standardized data, reliable interface modeling, and reproducible workflows across simulations and experiments.
paper_title: Breaking Bottlenecks in Solid Electrolyte Discovery with Large Artificial Intelligence Models
